fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title":"A Thousand Phantom Years","body":"Garton, who hosts Innerverse and Inner World alongside co host Dylan Sakosio, describes work ranging from biofield tuning and terrain based views of health to comparative mythology and philology. From there he argues that roughly a thousand years of accepted chronology never happened, tacked on to hide an already existing worldwide order. He cites Fomenko's charts, where a king reigns three years, is deposed in a specific way, and the identical sequence repeats beat by beat a thousand years later in another region, and he claims the first seven kings of Rome are simply the seven summer months."},{"title":"The Golden Thread of Baal","body":"Garton insists the name is closer to Bale, and that the Hebrew spelling, beth lamed, transliterates nearer to bol, which is to say bull. He splits the word into ba or ab for father and al for god, so Baal reads as father god, the same sense he finds in Jupiter, which he parses as Yahweh plus piter. He notes Augustine calling God Jove throughout City of God, Aaron's golden calf in Exodus, the Super Bowl as something set above the lord, and papal bulls declaring all kings subject to the pope, with B to L deity names running from Ireland to China."},{"title":"Atrocity Propaganda as Cover","body":"The pattern Garton describes is what he calls atrocity propaganda, where a shocking story stops people from examining real power. The Templars, accused of worshiping Baphomet, an idol drawn as a winged goat like blend of male and female, actually controlled banking and trade from Europe to Asia and are credited with paper currency; Garton suggests Baphomet was a name for Muhammad. He sees the same fingerprints, the 33s and hidden hands, pinned onto Freemasonry and NASA. Chris wonders whether the Epstein files work identically, a fire hose of dark information, and Garton replies that all warfare is worldview warfare."},{"title":"The Con at the Top","body":"Garton walks through the feudal pyramid of serfs, knights, lords and kings, then argues the real apex was the pope, since every king paid tithe to Rome. He says the structure persists because almost nobody holds allodial title, property tax and eminent domain turn owners into renters, and law still descends from canon law out of Rome. He calls Vatican City, Washington DC and the square mile City of London with its lord mayor the triple crown of Baal, with surveillance an honorable mention. The power at the top, he contends, is not sorcery but psychology, a con linking con, cohen and coin."},{"title":"Plato's Warning About Atlantis","body":"Garton points to a Texas university, he thinks Texas A&M, running an AI censorship program that stripped Plato from the curriculum over a passage about hermaphroditic humans split by Zeus, and he calls Plato the daddy of all philosophy. He retells Atlantis from the Timaeus and the Critias, a civilization of nine thousand years ago that derived its laws from Poseidon, and recommends Jack Kelly's documentary The Atlantis Puzzle. Read esoterically, he says, the myth warns that when a deeply traditional society meets a radically progressive one, both are destroyed, which is why philosophers concealed their truths."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: I joined Chris Mathieu on Forbidden Knowledge News to talk fake history, Baal symbolism, Atlantis, occult power structures, religious programming, and the hidden architecture of control still shaping the modern world. This one goes deep into empire, psychology, esotericism, and reclaiming spiritual sovereignty in an age of deception.
